title: Heat transfer with particles and waves
log: 2026-11-12T12:44:22Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new
2026-11-12T15:15:53Z write: the API refused it in the chapter request, so it is written on its own next

match.reason: No bank point teaches the particle model of conduction and convection together with the wave model of radiation through empty space; the closest, phys-heat-transfer, is a Physics Units 1 and 2 card covering all three heat transfer methods at a different depth and without the particle/wave model framing, and the conduction card covers only conduction.

draft.title: Heat transfer with particles and waves
card: Heat passes through a solid when fast-vibrating particles bump into their neighbours and pass on energy. The particles stay in place, and the energy moves.
In a liquid or gas, warmer parts spread out and rise, and cooler parts sink. The moving fluid carries heat with it, which sets up a circulating current.
Hot objects give off energy as waves. These waves can cross empty space with no particles, as sunlight does on its way to Earth.
Conduction and convection need particles. Radiation does not, so it is the only one of the three that works through a vacuum.
draft.remember: Conduction and convection pass heat through particles. Radiation carries it by waves.

a.q: A metal spoon is left in a hot pot of soup. The handle slowly gets hot. How does the heat travel along the spoon?
opts: Vibrating particles pass energy to their neighbours
Warm metal particles rise up the spoon as a current
Heat waves travel through the spoon from the soup
Metal particles flow from the bowl to the handle
a.why: The spoon is a solid, so its particles stay in place and pass on energy by bumping into neighbours. That is conduction. Convection is the tempting wrong answer, but it needs a liquid or gas that can flow, and a solid cannot.
a.clue: Solid particles can vibrate but cannot flow.

b.q: A camper in Mallacoota sits near a campfire. Her face feels warm even though the air between her and the fire is cool. What mainly carries the heat to her face?
opts: Radiation, as the fire gives off waves of energy
Convection, as warm air flows from the fire to her
Conduction, as air particles pass energy along
Conduction, as the fire touches her skin directly
b.why: The fire gives off energy as waves, which warm her face directly. That is radiation. Convection is tempting because hot air does rise from a fire, but it rises upwards, and the air between them is cool.
b.clue: Which type of heat transfer needs no particles to carry the energy?

a.best: Vibrating particles pass energy to their neighbours

b.best: Radiation, as the fire gives off waves of energy
